The Architect Behind the Words

How Rebbie Afuyaso built BettyWakiaBlog — from the PNG Wuhan and China Students Association sites to a calm, welcoming home for essays, research, and books.

I had seen Rebbie’s work before I ever spoke to him about my own. It’s hard not to notice the quiet hum of a well-built website when you’re scrolling through the Papua New Guinea student community pages.

I’m a researcher and a writer. My world is built on paragraphs, citations, and the slow, deliberate crafting of ideas. But Rebbie? He builds the vessels that carry those ideas to the world. I had watched him piece together the digital homes for the PNG Wuhan Students Association and the PNG China Students Association. They were clean, professional, and—most importantly—they felt like us. They weren’t just generic templates; they had soul, structure, and a clear understanding of the community they served.

I knew right then that if I ever wanted a place to gather my essays, my research notes, and my books, he was the only person I wanted to build it.

So, I reached out to him. I didn’t just ask for a website; I asked him to build my space. I told him I wanted it to feel calm, welcoming, and thoughtful—a place where readers could sit with an idea for a while. I wanted the books I’ve published to have a proper home, the research papers to be accessible, and the articles to be easy to find.

I handed him the vision, and Rebbie handed me the blueprint. We talked through the details: how the navigation should feel, the way the categories should be organized, and how important it was that the cover images actually loaded and looked beautiful. He didn’t just take my notes; he translated them into code. He built the structure, integrated the content management system so I could easily add my own work without touching a single line of code, and ensured that every page was optimized for search engines so my writing could reach the right people.

When he sent me the final link, it wasn’t just a website. It was a reflection of my work, elevated by his technical precision. The colors were bold, the layout was clean, and the navigation worked flawlessly. He delivered exactly what I asked for, and he did it with the same quiet dedication he brings to every project he touches.

Rebbie saw the potential in my words, and I saw the potential in his craft. Together, we built BettyWakiaBlog—a home for stories worth reading and books worth keeping. And honestly, I couldn’t have asked for a better architect to build it.
